question: Which layer actually bounds a play-test today, given post_playtest's default socket timeout is 4200 s (raised 2026-11-08)?
answer_summary: There are two real paths. (1) The godot_playtest tool / godot_compile chained playtest goes through post_playtest and is bounded by its 4200 s socket (impl.py:648, :705). (2) The repo gate (run_tests -> run_tests.sh -> game godot_gate.py -> sidecar /playtest) is bounded by the game gate's own /playtest socket of 3600 s (godot_gate.py:1816-1818 on the scratch copy), inside the 12600 s REPO_GATE_TIMEOUT relay (run_tests impl.py:1306). The largest completed render (3471.29 s, wuxia-godot-gate-7kf51nvv, passed) fired NO layer; on the repo-gate path the first layer to fire for a render that runs longer is the game gate's 3600 s socket, which had 128.7 s of headroom for it. The 4200 default raise does NOT lengthen the repo-gate path. The addon's 3900/3600 step budgets are claim-staleness windows in the engine, not kills (stepflow core.py:5732-5740). The 3600 s authored-scenario ceiling (impl.py:58) is a per-run clamp, not the socket.

first_to_fire.which_layer_fires_first_for_the_measured: No layer fired for the completed 3471.29 s render: it returned passed:true with no gate_timeout. On the path it took (repo gate), the bounds in order of tightness are: (a) the game gate's /playtest socket at 3600 s (godot_gate.py:1816-1818, scratch copy; headroom 3600 - 3471.2921 = 128.7079 s), (b) the relay queue window 1500 s (gate_admission.py:94; not reached: lock wait 0.0001 s), (c) REPO_GATE_TIMEOUT / relay upstream socket 12600 s (run_tests impl.py:1306, :1449; gate_admission.py:520; headroom 9128.7079 s). So for this render the FIRST bound that would fire is (a), the game-side 3600 s socket, with 128.7 s to spare; it is the layer that would have orphaned it had it run 129 s longer. If the same render had gone through post_playtest (4200 s socket, impl.py:705), headroom would be 728.7079 s.
first_to_fire.path_actually_taken: Attribution: the retained report sits in a gate directory with the stage layout and progress.log header of the game repo gate (manifest stages python/compile/playtest/script; gate-reports/wuxia-godot-gate-<id>/), written by godot_gate.py via GATE_REPORT_DIR (the scratch copy shows the mkdtemp 'wuxia-godot-gate-' prefix at godot_gate.py:1892). So the path is run_tests -> run_tests.sh -> game godot_gate.py -> sidecar /playtest, NOT a post_playtest call from this tree; the tree's 4200 s socket (impl.py:648) was not on that path. The 4200 default is the bound only for godot_playtest / godot_compile callers. Attribution rests on the stage layout and the scratch copy's prefix; the 2026-09-18 game-gate source is not retained, so it is an inference.

measured_worst.largest_aborted_note: NOT a completed measurement. The gate client was killed by the reroll-r1b driver and the sidecar drained (manifest note). It is a lower bound on the wall the sidecar handler held (6559.6 s). It exceeds the 4200 s post_playtest socket and the 3600 s game-gate socket, so on the repo-gate path it would have been orphaned at 3600 s (the client was in fact killed by the driver first). It is the only retained evidence of a render longer than 3600 s, and it did not complete.

mismatches.current_text: the real budget lives in post_playtest (3600s) plus the sidecar's 120s per scenario. Keep this just above that so the outer number can never be the one that fires first.
mismatches.chain_value: post_playtest default socket is 4200 s (impl.py:648); the 3600 s is AUTHORED_SCENARIO_CEILING_SEC (impl.py:58), a clamp on the authored caller budget, not the socket. For the repo-gate path the bound is REPO_GATE_TIMEOUT 12600 s (run_tests impl.py:1306).
mismatches.could_cut_real_play_test_short: No (for the measured render). Stale prose. The 3900 s value is not an enforced kill, so the 'outer number can never fire first' claim is not something the engine provides (L5).

mismatches.chain_value: The 5_compile step runs godot_compile, which chains godot_playtest at default 4200 s socket (godot_compile impl.py:309 -> impl.py:876). A 3900 s declared step budget is shorter than the 4200 s socket it contains, and it is only a claim-staleness window (stepflow core.py:5732-5740), not a kill.
mismatches.could_cut_real_play_test_short: Could mark the claim failed on the next advance_run if a playtest ran past 3900 s on the godot_compile path (4200 s socket). Not a kill; but a render between 3900 and 4200 s would be recorded as a step timeout while the report still lands. Caution, not a measured cut: the largest completed render is 3471.29 s, under 3900.

mismatches.chain_value: 5_vision does not POST /playtest; it judges frames from 5_compile. The 3600 figure is about the vision judge (its own comment: a healthy 69-scenario run took ~770 s). Its comment (:116-118) says 'a healthy 69-scenario run measured 770s', while the largest retained playtest is 166 scenarios / 3471 s.
mismatches.could_cut_real_play_test_short: No. It does not bound the play-test; the number is stale relative to the current 166-scenario contract.

mismatches.current_text: The game gate reads each render answer with one socket timeout (/script 1800 s, /playtest 3600 s).
mismatches.chain_value: The default post_playtest socket is 4200 s (impl.py:648), not 3600 s. The game gate's /playtest request is made by tools/godot_gate.py at line 1816-1818: transport("/playtest", {..."timeout": process_timeout, ...}, 3600). The 3600 is the HTTP socket (http_transport urlopen timeout, godot_gate.py:246-250), so the game gate does NOT use the 4200 socket. Provenance caveat: the only godot_gate.py readable here is the scratch copy /home/linxuhao/gate-window-20261107/wtree/tools/godot_gate.py (mtime 2026-11-07, git a65e8829), NOT the copy that produced the 2026-09-18 wuxia render; the 2026-09-18 client timeout is therefore not directly measured.
mismatches.could_cut_real_play_test_short: YES if the current game gate is the scratch copy: a play-test whose sidecar wall exceeds 3600 s is orphaned by the GAME GATE's own socket at 3600 s, before the 4200 s post_playtest socket (which the game gate does not use) can fire. The 3471.29 s render has 128.7 s headroom under that socket. The impl.py:641-647 comment and the 4200 raise do not protect the repo-gate path; the 12600 relay REPO_GATE_TIMEOUT is the outer bound but the 3600 client socket fires first.

mismatches.chain_value: Matches the game gate's client timeout in the scratch copy (godot_gate.py:1816-1818, transport(..., 3600)); the 1500 relay queue and 600 keepalive constants are the relay's own (gate_admission.py:94, :98). The /script 1800 figure is not re-verified here.
mismatches.could_cut_real_play_test_short: Same as M8: the 3600 s game-gate socket is the first repo-gate bound a render over 3600 s hits, on the scratch copy's evidence.

mismatches.current_text: (not a text claim; the sidecar's /playtest route defaults req.get('timeout', 120) at godot_harness.py:7585)

mismatches.current_text: 600s, not 180. ... Keep this comfortably under the 5_compile step's own timeout_seconds so the step budget, not this socket, is the bound.
